note: Teaching text, clarifying questions, inferred constraints and own examples. Inferred, not official. Examples are small generated inputs with outputs from the independent references in oracles.py.

constraints: file names are distinct, 1 to 30 characters from letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-"
lines are printable ASCII, at most 200 characters each
total lines <= 1e5 and total line characters <= 1e6
clarifyingQuestions: Does a match have to be a whole word, or does any substring count?
Is a line with several matches listed once or once per match?
In which order are files and lines reported?
Is case ignored only for ASCII letters?
hints: Lowercase the search word once.
Walk each line and cut it into maximal letter-or-digit runs; compare each run, lowercased, with the word.
Keep a per-file counter and the list of lines that matched; emit a row only when the counter is positive, with the count turned into a string.
invariants: a reported count equals the number of matching tokens in the reported lines
every reported line contains at least one matching token
chooseWhen: Grep-like reporting over in-memory text
tradeoffs: A hand-written tokenizer avoids regex engine differences between languages; a regex is shorter where both languages agree
hack2hire:68d8465eae12841706c1fc6e.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: case-insensitive whole-word search across files

constraints: keys are 1 to 4 characters, fields 1 to 8 characters, from lowercase letters and digits
values are 0 to 8 lowercase letters or digits; prefixes 0 to 8 such characters
clarifyingQuestions: Are later levels cumulative, and are earlier methods still called once timestamps are introduced?
How are scan results formatted and ordered?
Is a TTL interval half-open, so a field set at t with ttl d expires exactly at t + d?
Which backup does restore use, and how are remaining TTLs carried over?
hints: A record is a map from field to value; the database is a map from key to record.
getData must not create records; return "" when either level is missing.
deleteData reports whether something was actually removed.
invariants: each (key, field) pair holds at most one value
a scan lists each field at most once, in increasing field order
chooseWhen: Keyed record stores with per-field operations
tradeoffs: Nested hash maps make point operations O(1); a sorted map per record would make scans output-sensitive at the cost of slower writes
hack2hire:689505e73a1d9e6d6042d51a.variantLabel: Level 1: set, get and delete fields

Backups arrive in increasing time, so a list is already sorted; binary search finds the latest at or before the target.
Restoring rebuilds the maps and turns each remaining lifetime into restore time + remaining.

a scan lists each field at most once, in increasing field order
an expired field is never returned

clarifyingQuestions: What does poll or getRandom return on an empty queue?
Does getRandom remove the element?
How is randomness made testable: a seed, an injected index, or statistical checks?
hints: A linked list gives O(1) add and poll but not O(1) random access.
Store values in an array and keep the index of the front instead of shifting.
Position p from the front lives at head + p; compact the array occasionally so dead slots do not grow without bound.
invariants: size equals the number of adds minus the number of successful polls
the live values are exactly the array slots from head to the end
chooseWhen: FIFO buffers that also need uniform sampling
tradeoffs: A head index keeps every operation O(1); a circular buffer avoids compaction but needs resizing
hack2hire:677df76b052a260e0165706c.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: unbounded queue with O(1) indexed random access

constraints: after every map, the composed map a x + b satisfies |a| * max|arr| + |b| <= 1e15 (all values stay exact)
clarifyingQuestions: What can map take: arbitrary functions, or a fixed set of operations?
Does map return a new lazy array or change this one?
Should indexOf return the first index or any index?
How large can values grow after many multiplications?
hints: Composing add and multiply always gives a function of the form a x + b.
Precompute the first index of every original value.
indexOf solves a x + b = target: if a = 0 the answer is 0 or -1; otherwise the preimage exists only when a divides target - b.
invariants: after k maps the composed coefficients describe exactly the k transformations in order
the first-index table never changes
chooseWhen: Deferred pipelines where queries can be answered through the inverse transformation
tradeoffs: Composition is O(1) per map but only works for an invertible-by-algebra family; arbitrary functions force materializing the array
hack2hire:68539b6bd3dbd4fb8b026e9f.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: deferred affine maps with first-index lookup

clarifyingQuestions: Does each move cost energy, or only wall crossings?
Does re-crossing a wall cost again?
Is a wall at position 0 possible?
hints: An optimal route turns at most once: some walls on one side, back through them, then walls on the other side.
On each side, crossing the nearest walls first is forced, so prefix sums describe every choice.
For a fixed number on the first side the cost grows with the number on the other side, so two pointers (or binary search) find the best partner.
invariants: the walls crossed on each side are a prefix by distance
the first side is paid twice and the second side once
chooseWhen: Budgeted two-sided expansion with prefix costs
tradeoffs: Two pointers are linear after sorting; binary search per i is simpler to reason about at an extra log factor
hack2hire:697460b3a0697bac5fdca97e.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: maximize distinct walls with a one-turn route

clarifyingQuestions: What happens when a player in the last room solves its puzzle?
How are players in the same room ranked?
What exactly does a top-performer query return: ids, rooms or both?
hints: Players only move up by one room, so the set of occupied rooms changes locally.
Keep each room's players in entry order; a move appends to the next room's list.
Link the non-empty rooms in decreasing order and walk them from the top until k players are collected.
invariants: the per-room counts sum to m
each room list is ordered by entry time
the non-empty room list is sorted and contains exactly the rooms with count > 0
chooseWhen: Leaderboards where scores only increase by one step
tradeoffs: Linked lists give O(k) queries; a heap or balanced tree handles arbitrary score jumps at O(log m) per update
hack2hire:681bc967a73bd75b806cb994.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: room leaderboard with arrival-order ties

clarifyingQuestions: Is an event exactly window seconds after the last print allowed?
Do suppressed events restart the cooldown?
What should the method return?
hints: Only the last printed time of each name matters.
Suppressed events do not change any state.
Compare timestamp - last against window and update only on print.
invariants: the stored time for a name is the time of its latest printed event
chooseWhen: Per-key throttling of monotone event streams
tradeoffs: A map of last times is O(names); evicting old names needs an extra queue but saves memory on long streams
hack2hire:68edc9c15abdefad4f6693fc.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: per-name cooldown logger

constraints: all rows have the same length, 0 to 1000
keys are 1 to 10 characters from lowercase letters, digits and "_"
values are 0 to 10 characters from lowercase letters, digits, "_" and ":"
clarifyingQuestions: If one source lists the same key twice, which entry wins?
Is the result a map, or a list, and in what order?
Can a key be empty?
hints: Splitting at the first colon keeps colons inside the value.
Processing in preference order means the last write for a key is the final value.
Collect the map, then sort its keys and rebuild "key:value" strings.
invariants: after processing a prefix of entries the map holds, per key, the latest entry in that prefix
chooseWhen: Layered configuration merging
tradeoffs: A forward overwrite pass is simplest; a reverse pass with first-wins can stop early once all keys are known
hack2hire:6a987edf0ca9cc4e1c78a9a5.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: last write wins by source preference

constraints: start and end follow the format exactly
a range spans less than one week (at most 2016 outputs)
clarifyingQuestions: Are times aligned to multiples of 5 or stepped from start?
Are both ends inclusive?
What if end is earlier in the week than start?
Is the hour zero-padded?
hints: Map each time to minutes since Monday 12:00 AM.
Round the start up to a multiple of 5; if end is smaller, add one week to it.
Step by 5 minutes and convert back, taking the result modulo one week and using 12 for hour 0.
invariants: every emitted minute value is a multiple of 5 and lies in the (possibly wrapped) range
chooseWhen: Enumerating schedule slots in a cyclic week
tradeoffs: Integer minutes avoid date libraries; a library would be needed for real calendars with time zones
hack2hire:6782d18f3cd890ccd3798fc5.variantLabel: Inferred single variant: aligned 5-minute times in a weekly range

clarifyingQuestions: Are words distinct?
What should be returned when no word fits?
Can s be shorter than every word?
hints: A substring is an anagram of a word exactly when both have the same 26 letter counts.
All words of the same length can share one sliding window over s.
Encode the window counts as an exact key and look it up among word keys of that length; keep the smallest word index found.
invariants: the window key always equals the counts of the current window of fixed length
chooseWhen: Multi-pattern anagram search
tradeoffs: Sharing windows by length avoids one pass per word; exact count keys avoid hash false positives
hack2hire:68c8719bdf5a6365aa774b15.variantLabel: Single variant: first word whose anagram occurs in s

clarifyingQuestions: Is "at least k" or "exactly k" distinct required?
What is returned when no subarray qualifies?
hints: If a window has at least k distinct values, so does every window containing it.
Use two pointers with a count per value.
After each extension, shrink from the left while the window stays good, recording the length each time.
invariants: distinct equals the number of values with positive count in the window
chooseWhen: Minimum-length windows with a monotone property
tradeoffs: Two pointers are linear; binary search on the length with a fixed window is O(n log n)
hack2hire:69f131b096981f58ae1f7654.variantLabel: Single variant: shortest window with at least k distinct values

clarifyingQuestions: How is the tree given as input?
Must the path end at a leaf?
With repeated values, is any matching branch enough?
hints: Because values repeat, several nodes can match the same prefix.
Keep the whole frontier of matching nodes for each depth.
Each node is examined at most once, at its own depth.
invariants: the frontier at step i contains exactly the depth-i nodes whose root chain matches path[0..i]
chooseWhen: Pattern lookup along root paths with duplicate labels
tradeoffs: A frontier search is iterative and depth-safe; recursion is shorter but limited by stack depth

clarifyingQuestions: Can the path start below the root?
Must it go strictly downward?
hints: Every root-to-node chain is a string of values; the question is whether path is a substring ending at some node.
Run KMP along each root chain; children resume from their parent's state.
Branching breaks KMP's amortization, so memoize the automaton transition for each (state, value) pair.
invariants: the state at a node is the longest path prefix that is a suffix of its root chain
chooseWhen: Substring search over every root-to-node string of a tree
tradeoffs: Memoized KMP transitions avoid repeated failure walks; trying every start is simpler but quadratic
hack2hire:6772e85ddd9437f8aa275b02.variantLabel: Inferred variant 2: downward path starting anywhere
